source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India Since Independence, Ch. 1 (Challenges of Nation Building).

sections.heading: 1. The Three Challenges at Independence
points: At Independence (1947), India faced three major challenges:

sub: **Unity in diversity** — to shape one nation from immense diversity of religion, language, region.
**Democracy** — to establish democratic institutions and practice.
**Development and equity** — to ensure development that benefited all.

sections.heading: 2. Partition and Its Consequences
points: The **Partition of 1947** (based on the 'two-nation theory') created India and Pakistan.
It caused **massive violence, displacement (~millions), and refugee crises** — one of the largest, most violent migrations in history.
The problem of **minorities** on both sides, and the challenge of secularism, arose.

sections.heading: 3. Integration of Princely States
points: There were ~**565 princely states**; most acceded to India after Independence.
**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** (with V.P. Menon) played the key role in **integrating the princely states** (through persuasion and the Instrument of Accession).
Difficult cases: **Junagadh, Hyderabad (Operation Polo), and Jammu & Kashmir**.
This preserved India's territorial unity.

sections.heading: 4. Reorganisation of States
points: Demand for **linguistic states** (states drawn on the basis of language).
The death of **Potti Sriramulu** (hunger strike) led to the creation of **Andhra Pradesh (1953)**.
The **States Reorganisation Commission (1953)** → the **States Reorganisation Act (1956)** redrew state boundaries on a linguistic basis.
Linguistic reorganisation strengthened, not weakened, national unity.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three challenges: unity in diversity, democracy, development/equity.
Partition (1947) = massive violence and displacement.
Sardar Patel (with V.P. Menon) integrated ~565 princely states.
Potti Sriramulu's death → Andhra Pradesh (1953, first linguistic state).
States Reorganisation Act (1956) = linguistic states.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Sardar Patel** led the **integration of the princely states**.
**Andhra Pradesh (1953)** was the first state formed on a **linguistic** basis (after Potti Sriramulu).
The **States Reorganisation Act was in 1956**.
**Hyderabad's integration** was through **Operation Polo**.
